name: Opendoor: consumer landing page for its cash offer home-selling service
title: Opendoor: consumer landing page for its cash offer home-selling service
answer: This is Opendoor's consumer homepage, a marketing page for homeowners who want to sell without listing, showings or repairs. It says Opendoor uses real-time data, advanced pricing algorithms and on-the-ground expertise to set an offer, weighing comparable sales, market conditions and the home's features and condition. The most useful detail for an AI reader is that an estimated cash offer arrives within 24 hours and a final offer follows a home assessment within a few days. The page gives no information about the models themselves.

sections.body: Opendoor publishes this page, which is the company's consumer-facing homepage rather than a report, filing or technical document. Its scope is the home-selling offer: what the offer includes, how it is calculated, how long it takes and how a seller can cancel. The page names Opendoor Labs Inc. in its accessibility statement. No publication or revision date is stated in the harvested text, and the only figures given are a customer count and a cost range.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: The page presents Opendoor as a way to sell a home without listing, showings or months of stress, closing on the seller's own timeline. A seller enters an address and a few details and receives an estimated cash offer within 24 hours. After a home assessment, Opendoor sends a final offer within a few days. The final offer is broken into parts: the purchase price for the home, a program fee for selling without staging or showings, a condition adjustment to cover the cost of preparing and reselling the home, title and escrow costs of 1 to 3 percent paid to third parties, and the estimated net proceeds after all costs. Opendoor says it determines the offer using real-time data, advanced pricing algorithms and on-the-ground expertise, analysing comparable home sales in the area, current market conditions, and the home's specific features and condition. Sellers can cancel any time before closing without cost or penalty by contacting a Customer Experience Partner. The page also promotes a Cash Now, More Later option, described as giving the convenience of a cash offer with the proceeds of a market transaction. Three customer testimonials praise the speed, fairness and lack of hassle, and an accessibility statement invites contact at a support address.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: The page states that over 310,113 homeowners have been served by Opendoor. It gives title and escrow costs as 1 to 3 percent, paid to third parties. It says an estimated cash offer comes within 24 hours and a final offer within a few days after the home assessment. It claims sellers can cancel any time before closing without cost or penalty. It lists the components of a final offer: purchase price, program fee, condition adjustment, title and escrow costs, and estimated net proceeds. No accuracy figures, model performance data or financial results appear.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: A reader following AI in real estate would use this page as the public description of a pricing system with money at stake, since Opendoor states that advanced pricing algorithms help set the offer a seller is paid. It shows how an automated valuation is presented to consumers, as an estimated offer followed by a final offer after an assessment, and how the resulting price is split into fees and adjustments. It is a starting point for the consumer-facing side of algorithmic home pricing, not an account of how the models work or how they perform.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Real Estate

sections.body: This is a commercial marketing page, so it promotes the service and does not evaluate it. It contains no filings, financial statements, model documentation, error rates or independent evidence, and it does not mention balance-sheet exposure or risk. The only numbers are a customer count, a cost range and two timeframes. No date is given, so the figures may be out of date. The testimonials are selected customer comments. Anyone wanting the record of valuation models with capital consequences would need Opendoor's filings and technical documentation, which this page is not.
